transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO - Pinecrest), Mark Chen (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Security), Sam Brooks (Product)

00:00 Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for the time. I'm Ava, AE on the account, and with me is Jon from our SE team. Quick thumbcheck — is everyone seeing my screen?
00:18 Lena Ortiz: Yes, we can see it. Thanks Ava. We have about 45 minutes. Want to focus on how you do org and project keys, rate limits, and the multi-tenant controls because that's the gating concern for us.
00:30 Ava: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll cover. Jon will run the demo and I'll jump in for pricing/contract stuff.
00:36 Jon Park: Cool. I'll start with a high-level: Redwood has a two-tier key model — org keys for global admin operations and project keys scoped to individual teams or apps.
00:50 Jon Park: (screen) Here is the Console. At the org level you can set account-wide quotas, billing, and SSO integrations. Then you create projects under the org with project-level keys that inherit some policies but can have overrides — like per-project rate limits and usage quotas.
01:05 Mark Chen: Quick question — if a project exceeds its quota, does it fail hard or is there a soft-fail/queued mode?
01:12 Jon Park: Good question. We support configurable enforcement — you can do hard rejects, token-based throttling with 429s, or a soft degraded mode that routes to a lower-capacity model variant. There's also burst policies for short spikes.
01:30 Priya Nair: From a security standpoint we need audit logs per key and also key rotation. Do you support KMS and HSM-backed keys?
01:40 Jon Park: Yes, you can bring your own KMS or use Redwood-managed keys. Audit logs are available at org and project levels; they record key usage at token and request granularity and are exportable to S3 or our SIEM connectors.
01:58 Ava Martinez: And we include RBAC — so you can assign admin vs billing vs read-only at org/project scopes. That helps with least privilege for teams.
02:12 Lena Ortiz: How do you handle multi-tenant billing? We need per-team budgeting and chargebacks.
02:20 Jon Park: In the Console we have project-level usage breakdowns (tokens, embeddings, requests) and you can attach billing codes to projects. You can also set hard quotas so teams won't exceed budget.
02:32 Sam Brooks: If a rogue job starts hammering the API in a single project, can we throttle that project without impacting the org?
02:39 Jon Park: Exactly — project-level rate limits are enforced independently. You can also configure fallback policies to route to hosted lower-cost model or circuit-break the project only.
02:52 Mark Chen: What's the granularity of rate limiting? Per minute, per second? Per key?
03:00 Jon Park: We support per-second and per-minute windows, plus dynamic token-bucket shapes. Limits can be applied per-project key or per-route (if you want different limits for embeddings vs generation).
03:14 Ava Martinez: For enterprise customers we also offer Dedicated pools which give isolated capacity and SLA. That helps for noisy neighbors. But most customers start on Hosted with strict project limits.
03:26 Lena Ortiz: Our compliance team strongly prefers on-prem or VPC deployments. How does rate limiting behave in Private deployments?
03:36 Jon Park: Private deployments mirror the same control plane — org/project keys, quotas, and metrics — but the runtime is local. You still get the same enforcement, and logs remain within the VPC. There are small differences in telemetry export options because of network constraints.
03:49 Priya Nair: Do rate limits appear in logs so we can alert on quota near-thresholds?
03:55 Jon Park: Yes, we emit events for quota thresholds and 429 spikes. You can hook them into our Console alerts or forward to PagerDuty.
04:04 Ava Martinez: I'll pause for a sec — Jon, can you demo creating an org and a project key and applying a limit?
04:09 Jon Park: Sure. (click) Creating org: Pinecrest-Prod. Creating project: patient-annotations. Now generate project key. Here on the policy tab, I'll add a rate limit: 10 requests/second, 1000 requests/minute, and a monthly quota of 5M tokens.
04:40 Mark Chen: When you set that limit, is it enforced at the edge or at the runtime? We have concerns about latency for 429s.
04:48 Jon Park: Enforcement is at the gateway edge within the same region — we aim for sub-millisecond checks; the runtime doesn't add round-trip. There's a local cache for policies so checks don't hit the control plane each time.
05:02 Sam Brooks: You mentioned overrides — can product teams self-serve to request temporary quota increases?
05:09 Jon Park: Yes. Projects can submit quota increase requests which go to the org admins. We also have an autoscale/burst feature that can provision temporary capacity from a shared pool under policy constraints.
05:22 Lena Ortiz: What's the model for billing when a project bursts? Charge to the project or org-level pooled billing?
05:29 Ava Martinez: You can configure it either way. By default, burst usage is billed to the org but we provide per-project attribution so you can run chargebacks. For Dedicated, you can set reserved capacity and then chargebacks are based on usage within the reservation.
05:44 Mark Chen: Any chance to get a CSV export of per-key usage for our finance team?
05:49 Jon Park: Yes, exports are available from the Console for any time window and can be auto-scheduled.
06:00 Jon Park: (small pause) Now I'll run a quick live test — I'll use a test harness to send 200 concurrent requests to the project key and show how the rate limits kick in.
06:08 Jon Park: (runs script) You can see traffic graph, and at 07:12 we start hitting 429s for one worker because we've set 10 rps; overall throughput stabilizes at the policy threshold.
06:20 Mark Chen: I see some errors — the error messages look a bit different from what our SDK expects. Can we customize 429 payloads?
06:28 Jon Park: We support custom error payloads and headers so your SDK can handle retries gracefully. Also include Retry-After header and a JSON reason code.
06:37 Priya Nair: Any mitigation for sudden traffic from compromised keys? For example, auto-rotate or quarantining keys?
06:45 Jon Park: We have a kill-switch to revoke a key immediately. We also have anomaly detection that can flag unusual per-key patterns and automatically throttle or quarantine until a manual review.
06:58 Ava Martinez: For contractual concerns, Pinecrest mentioned SLA on request success and latency. For Hosted tier we publish SLOs and for Dedicated we can offer SLA-backed latency targets.
07:12 Lena Ortiz: Can you share a sample policy we can plug into our runbooks — something that calls out thresholds and alerting?
07:20 Jon Park: I'll drop a sample policy file to the chat. (typing) Sending: "sample-quota-policy.yaml".
07:28 Ava Martinez: We'll include that in the follow-up pack.
07:32 Sam Brooks: One more product question — do you support per-route quotas so embeddings consumption doesn't starve generation?
07:40 Jon Park: Absolutely. You can create route filters like path=/v1/embeddings and set separate qps and token quotas.
07:48 Mark Chen: How are keys rotated? Can we automate rotation on a schedule via API?
07:52 Jon Park: Yes, keys support TTL and scheduled rotation via the API or Console. You can use your KMS to store the root material.
08:02 Priya Nair: About audit logs — is there a retention policy and can we archive beyond default?
08:09 Jon Park: Default retention is 90 days in Console; you can configure long-term archiving to S3 for indefinite storage, and export events to your SIEM with attribute-level filters.
08:20 Lena Ortiz: Let's talk integration — we have a CI job that spins up thousands of short-lived jobs. We don't want them to exhaust org quotas. Best practice?
08:30 Jon Park: Recommended pattern: give CI its own project and conservative per-minute limits; use short-lived project keys with low quotas; set hard rejects for non-prod environments. Also use policy-driven preflight checks in the SDK.
08:44 Mark Chen: In your demo earlier you mentioned model fallback — what's the cost implication?
08:49 Jon Park: Fallback routes to a lower-cost model; usage still counted but at the model used. Many customers prefer fallback to preserve UX while saving costs, but you can also circuit-break.
08:58 Ava Martinez: Switching to the commercial side — there are two SKU families: Hosted consumption and Dedicated reserved. Rate-limit controls and project keys are available in both. Dedicated adds guaranteed throughput.
09:12 Lena Ortiz: If we start a pilot, what does onboarding look like? Can we get a sandbox tenant with a couple project keys to run our perf tests?
09:20 Ava Martinez: Yes. Jon will provision a sandbox org and two project keys after the call; we'll also send a starter guide and sample workloads.
09:29 Jon Park: I'll note that. Provisioning should be done within 24 hours.
09:33 Sam Brooks: For acceptance criteria, we need less than 100ms p50 for generation on our normal jobs and predictable throttling semantics during peak.
09:43 Jon Park: Got it. We'll include a benchmark harness. Can you share three workloads and target p50/p95?
09:50 Mark Chen: We'll send that today.
09:53 Priya Nair: Security deep-dive — we need SOC 2 attestation and details on where logs live. Also SAML integration.
10:02 Ava Martinez: We'll attach SOC 2 report and a security FAQ. For SAML, our IdP integrations are in the Console and we can do an SSO test in the sandbox.
10:12 Lena Ortiz: Any gotchas for regional data residency? We have PHI constraints — need logs and token data to stay in US-East.
10:20 Jon Park: You can pin org to a region; for Hosted we have region options and for Private we can deploy inside your VPC or on-prem. PHI-sensitive workloads are usually on Dedicated or Private.
10:32 Mark Chen: One more — what about per-tenant differential quotas? e.g., within a single project we'd like to enforce per-customer sub-quotas.
10:40 Jon Park: We don't have built-in sub-project keys yet, but you can implement sub-tenant tagging on requests and use policy engines to apply quotas per tag. We also have a roadmap item for sub-project keys later next quarter.
10:55 Ava Martinez: Ok, quick recap. Action items: we will send pricing and policies, Jon will provision sandbox and keys, Pinecrest will send workloads and security questions. Next call — security deep-dive scheduled the week of 12/21.
11:10 Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Thanks Ava, Jon.
11:14 Ava Martinez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the pack.
11:18 (call ends)
notes: Demo was product-forward; customer is enterprise-sized healthcare org with PHI concerns. SE showed live rate-limit enforcement and discussed Dedicated options. Customer asked for SOC2, KMS, region pinning, and per-project quotas. Some minor transcription errors in proper nouns (e.g., 'InferEdge' might be mis-heard) and occasional overlap in crosstalk.
